recentItems.title: Taiwan's army trains with Stinger missile simulator amid focus on China's drone threats
recentItems.description:
(22 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Tainan, Taiwan -  22 September 2026
1. Wide of training drill, soldiers operating Stinger missile simulator
2. Solider operating Stinger missile simulator, monitor shows simulated battlefield
3. Close-up of soldier looking through viewfinder on the simulator 
4. Zoom-in of soldier firing simulated missile during training 
5. Close-up of soldier putting on VR goggle
6. Various of solider operating Stinger missile simulator 
7. Cutaway of soldier using computer 
8. Zoom-in of soldier operating Stinger missile simulator 
9. Wide Lt. Col. Chen Yu-wen speaking to journalists 
10. SOUNDBITE (Mandarin) Lt. Col. Chen Yu-wen of Army Artillery Training Department:
"After equipping our soldiers with basic system operation skills, we use the Stinger missile simulation system to train them in a simulated battlefield environment, teaching them how to operate the Stinger missile system and its operational procedures."
11. Various of Chen overseeing Stinger simulator training 
12. SOUNDBITE (Mandarin) Lt. Col. Chen Yu-wen of Army Artillery Training Department:
"Therefore, we have also set relevant drone parameters in the simulator system. We can use simulation training to familiarize soldiers with operational skills."
13. Various of army briefing of HIMARS rocket system 
14. Various of HIMARS rocket system 
15. Various of Taiwan-made Sky Sword anti-air missile system
STORYLINE:
Taiwan’s Army conducted training on Tuesday using a Stinger missile simulator at its artillery training command in southern Tainan, as the military seeks to strengthen its ability to counter low-altitude threats like drones from China.

The simulator was developed by Taiwan’s National Chung-Shan Institute of Science and Technology, or NCSIST, at the Army’s request.

It is designed to replicate battlefield conditions and allow troops to practice operating the Stinger missile system without live-fire launches. 

The Ministry of National Defense said the simulator incorporates visual and audio effects to reproduce combat conditions and familiarize soldiers with Stinger operating procedures, engagement techniques and battlefield responses.

Lt. Col. Chen Yu-wen, who oversees simulator training at the Army Artillery Training Department, said they have set relevant drone parameters in the simulator system as well. 

"We can use simulation training to familiarize soldiers with operational skills," he added.

Taiwan plans to acquire 2,621 additional Stinger missiles from the United States in two phases. Taiwan’s military already operates several versions of the Stinger, including man-portable systems, a dual-mount configuration and the U.S.-made Avenger air defense system. 

AP Video shot by Johnson Lai

recentItems.description:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Narsarsuaq, Greenland - 12 August 2025

20. Plane arriving at airport
21. Tracking shot walking towards plane on runway 
22. Wide of turboprop planes on runway
23. Tracking shot walking towards plane on runway 
24. People boarding plane 
25. Side view of plane 
26. View from plane as it takes off from runway 
27. View of mountains from plane
STORYLINE:
The United States of America, Denmark, and Greenland are set to sign an agreement later today aimed at strengthening Arctic and North Atlantic security, easing tensions that erupted over President Donald Trump's repeated calls for Greenland to become part of the United States. 

Danish public broadcaster DR reported Tuesday that the agreement involves the establishment of two new U.S. bases in Greenland and noted that the U.S. has repeatedly shown interest in the airport at the Narsarsuaq settlement in southern Greenland. 

The governments did not provide details of the accord ahead of a signing ceremony on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York later on Tuesday.

The agreement appeared set to reduce tensions between the U.S., Denmark and the European Union that erupted over Trump's repeated calls for Greenland to become part of the United States. 

For months, Trump expressed his desire for Greenland to become part of the United States, and issued threats to seize the semiautonomous territory of Denmark, a NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) ally.

For decades, the United States had a far larger presence in Greenland. 

Since 1945, the U.S. military presence in Greenland has decreased from thousands of soldiers across more than 17 bases and installations on the island to just the remote Pituffik Space Base in the northwest with roughly 200 soldiers today. 

AP video shot by James Brooks

recentItems.title: Kyiv residents view Zelenskyy-Trump meeting with scepticism in aftermath of latest Russian strike
recentItems.description:
(22 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Kyiv, Ukraine - 22 September 2026
1. Various of damaged residential building
2. Various of Iryna Panina cleaning debris from her apartment
3. Various of debris inside damaged apartment
4. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Iryna Panina, 36, Kyiv resident:
"It’s a matter of seconds - you don’t have time to get away or take cover. There’s an explosion, followed by a blast wave that tore out the window and pulled the rest of the debris down with it. Thank God, I’m alive and unharmed."
5. Mid of rubble
6. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Iryna Panina, 36, Kyiv resident:
"There’s been no hope in all these meetings, all these negotiations for a while now, because everything has dragged on for far too long. There have been no specific results from these talks or meetings. As an ordinary person just trying to live and survive each day, I find it hard to believe they fully understand what’s actually happening, how hard it is, and how much ordinary people are suffering."
7. Mid of rubble
8. Mid of man standing in front of broken window
9. Mid of Oleksandr Kondratiuk cleaning rubble
10. Mid of damaged kitchen
11. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Oleksandr Kondratiuk, 56, Kyiv resident:
"We feel very badly about these attacks, and the longer it goes on, the worse and worse it gets. I don’t know when it will end. Everyone is waiting for something to change because there is no strength left."
12. Mid view of yard from damaged apartment
13. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Oleksandr Kondratiuk, 56, Kyiv resident:
"I am already having doubts. Honestly, it seems to me that other people need to be appointed to conduct the negotiations. Because, well, I don’t [believe] Trump, and I can see that Volodymyr Zelenskyy is banging his head against a wall. There need to be some other people, not from our country, but from other countries who are also interested in ending the war. As I understand it, they want to wipe out the Ukrainian people and divide all of this here. That is how it seems to me."
14. Mid of damaged residential building
15. Various of Vasyl Nikonenko throwing broken glass into garbage
16. Mid of  damage
17. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Vasyl Nikonenko, 73, pensioner from Mariupol: 
"It becomes dulled, this feeling of fear. My wife is very afraid, very afraid. I’m afraid for her, that during another explosion she might drop dead."
18. Mid of damage
19. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Vasyl Nikonenko, 73, pensioner from Mariupol: "Trump is not the kind of man with whom it is possible to negotiate. He has finances on his mind. That’s all."
20. Various of local resident holding a dog
21. Wide of local residents
STORYLINE:
Kyiv residents were dealing with the aftermath of another Russian strike Tuesday that injured five people and damaged homes.

Iryna Panina, 36, woke at around 2 a.m. to the sound of a jet-powered Shahed drone during the Russian attack on Kyiv’s Dniprovskyi district.

Russia is now using jet-powered Shahed drones in large numbers, while Ukraine has yet to intercept them as effectively as the slower, propeller-driven versions.

“It’s a matter of seconds — you don’t have time to get away or take cover. There’s an explosion, followed by a blast wave that tore out the window and pulled the rest of the debris down with it,” Panina said.

Panina escaped unharmed.

“There has been no hope in all these meetings and negotiations for a while now,” she said, referring to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s trip to the United States. She said international efforts to end the war have dragged on for too long without producing concrete results.

ASSOCIATED PRESS

1. Entrance to Lourdes sanctuary with Basilica of Our Lady of Immaculate Conception

7. SOUNDBITE (English) Marco Politi, Vatican Analyst, Author of His Holiness: John Paul II and the Hidden History of our Time:
“This trip to France and also to Lourdes, which is a place where you feel the healing of God, is a moment in which Pope Leo wants to underscore the importance of Europe and the role in world politics of the European Union. Pope Francis had neglected Western Europe. So Pope Leo has decided now to care again also about Western Europe.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS
ARCHIVE: Lourdes, France – 17 August 1983
8. Pope John Paul II waving to crowd from Popemobile at Mass in Lourdes
9. Pope John Paul II walking up to altar area and waving to crowd

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Rome – 14 September 2025
10. SOUNDBITE (English) Marco Politi, Vatican Analyst, Author of His Holiness: John Paul II and the Hidden History of our Time:
“Pope John Paul II spoke to the people, to the believers, to the crowd about peace, justice. He encouraged the Catholics not to yield to atheism, to materialism. Not to turn too many problems about the mystery of the faith, it was a triumph for him."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
ARCHIVE: Rome – 14 August 2004
11. Pope John Paul II leaves Rome for trip to Lourdes, he is unable to walk, so he is using a special armchair/wheelchair

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Rome – 14 September 2025
12. SOUNDBITE (English) Marco Politi, Vatican Analyst, Author of His Holiness John Paul II and the Hidden History of our Time:
“John Paul II, when he went again to Lourdes in the year 2004, it was a dramatic experience. He had the Parkinson's, it was very strong, and he barely could speak."

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
ARCHIVE: Lourdes, France – 13 September 2008
++4:3++
13. Pope Benedict XVI in Lourdes

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Rome – 14 September 2025
14. SOUNDBITE (English) Marco Politi, Vatican Analyst, Author of His Holiness John Paul II and the Hidden History of our Time:
“Later on, Pope Benedict, when he went to Lourdes in the year 2008, said that Lourdes is a special place where you meet the loving face of God and you share the service for the suffering people.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
ARCHIVE: Lourdes, France – 13 September 2008
++4:3++
15. Pope Benedict in the Grotto of the Apparitions of Massabielle
16. Tilt up of Pope Benedict XVI

STORYLINE:
As preparations are underway at the Lourdes sanctuary for the visit of Pope Leo XIV, many of the faithful are looking back at visits of past popes. 

When the 63-year-old Pope John Paul II visited in 1983, he was full of energy, warmly greeting the faithful and bounding up to the altar to lead a three-hour Mass. The relatively young Pope had survived an assassination attempt and credited the Virgin Mary for saving his life. He had recently returned from a trip to Poland where he had met with Polish solidarity leaders and pressured Wojciech Jaruzelski to end martial law. According to Vatican expert Marco Politi, who covered the trip, John Paul II inspired the crowd, encouraging them not to give in to atheism or materialism.



Pope Leo XIV, however, is eager to focus once again on Catholics in Europe, according to experts.

recentItems.title: China daily MOFA briefing highlights
recentItems.description:
(22 Sep 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Beijing, China - 22 September 2026
Duration: 1 min 33 seconds
Spokesperson: Guo Jiakun

1. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned on Monday that Iranian airlines would find it difficult to operate globally under U.S. sanctions pressure. He said that starting tomorrow, all global routes operated by Iranian airlines would be grounded, and any country that provides services or fuel to Iranian airlines would be kicked out of the U.S. dollar system. It has been reported that Iranian flights are still scheduled to land in Guangzhou and Shanghai tomorrow morning. Will China continue to accept these Iranian flights?

China has always opposed illegal unilateral sanctions that lack a basis in international law and authorization from the UN Security Council.

2. At China’s invitation, Prime Minister of Malaysia Anwar Ibrahim will attend the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Competition and the launching ceremony of the Global Digital Trade Expo this week. What are China’s expectations for his visit? 

Prime Minister Anwar’s visit to China to attend activities related to the WorldSkills Competition and the Global Digital Trade Expo demonstrates the close and friendly relations between China and Malaysia, as well as the sound cooperation between the two sides in related areas. 
China looks forward to working with Malaysia to further deepen the alignment of development strategies, advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, strengthen communication and coordination on international and regional issues, and promote the building of a high-level strategic China-Malaysia community with a shared future so as to achieve more results.

3. The spokesperson office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today released a video on social media titled “Constructive Strategic Stability.” What are the main considerations and purpose behind the release of this video as President Xi Jinping is about to pay a state visit to the U.S.? what message does China hope to convey to the U.S. side and the international community?

Thank you for your attention to the Foreign Ministry’s social media accounts. China stands ready to work with the U.S. to enrich the substance of a constructive strategic stability relationship between the two countries, strengthen dialogue and cooperation, properly manage differences, continuously improve the well-being of the two peoples, and promote peace, stability and prosperity in the world.
STORYLINE:

ASSOCIATED PRESS

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Rio de Janeiro, Brazil – 24 August 2026
6. SOUNDBITE (Portuguese) Maria Isabel Couto, Director of Data and Transparency at Fogo Cruzado Institute: 
"Over the last decades, we had the development of airports and ports in Brazil that diversified from routes by which drugs can leave Brazil for the European market. Bahia lies in a kind of junction between these two routes."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Salvador, Brazil – 29 August 2026

ASSOCIATED PRESS

8. Police carrying guns patrolling on motorbikes through a favela

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Rio de Janeiro, Brazil – 24 August 2026
11. SOUNDBITE (Portuguese) Maria Isabel Couto, Director of Data and Transparency at Fogo Cruzado Institute: 
"Every state that becomes a strategic trading post for traffic also becomes highly contested by the organized crime groups. So you see these states with rising violence. It doesn’t mean those are violent states or territories by nature; these are territories hit by those groups and also by the state’s reaction in many cases."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Salvador, Brazil – 28 August 2026
12. Various of Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva campaigning with re-election candidate for governor of Bahia, Jerônimo Rodrigues
13. Crowd cheering during the campaign event
14. SOUNDBITE (Portuguese) Tiali Doria, Physical education teacher: 
"Not only here in Bahia do we have this public security problem, but I think that Lula thinks about public security as effective policies that take care of the citizen, not always as repression by the State. We need humanized public policies, and I think that is what Lula’s government promotes, not as an arm of the State that represses without public policies to change lives."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Salvador, Brazil – 29 August 2026
15. People taking pictures in front of the Lacerda Elevator, a known tourist spot in the city
16. Salvador’s historical Pelourinho neighborhood
17. View of the Gamboa neighborhood

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Salvador, Brazil – 16 September 2026
18. SOUNDBITE (Portuguese) Magnólia Nascimento, sister of Evilásio Santos: 
“I’ve been using social programs and using them well. In the future, when I’m back to work and not in need of social programs anymore, I’ll thank my government.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Salvador, Brazil – 29 August 2026
19. Silhouette of a group jumping from a rock into the sea during sunset
STORYLINE:
On the day they were going to kill him, Evilásio Santos da Silveira Júnior, 33, told his sister he was going grocery shopping in the city of Salvador in northern Brazil, where the line between the crossfire of rival drug gangs and police lethality has been increasingly blurred. 

But he never came back home. Bahia state police officers at the scene said he was caught in a shootout between rival factions and suspected him of involvement. His family said he had no ties to gangs and was instead randomly killed by state forces during an unprovoked surprise raid.

recentItems.title: Chinese analyst and Beijing residents preview Xi's visit to Washington to meet Trump
recentItems.description:
(22 Sep 2026)

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
ARCHIVE: Beijing, China - 14 May 2026
1. Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump inspecting honor guards during welcoming ceremony
2. Various of Xi and Trump waving to children who are waving flowers and chanting “Welcome!” 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 

Beijing, China - 16 September 2026
++OVERLAYED BY 1, 2 AND 4++
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Da Wei, Director of the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University: 
“I think the bilateral relations are kind of relatively stable. Of course, some bad news still happens, some frictions between the two sides,  but the overall stability remains. So I think we are at a moment that we need more meat on bone. I'm a little bit concerned that after the May summit, I think we have moved too slowly, the two sides. We should not squander time. The clock is ticking, so we need to move fast." 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
ARCHIVE: Beijing, China - 15 May 2026
4. Wide of Trump and Xi sitting for a meeting in Zhongnanhai garden

ASSOCIATED PRESS 

ARCHIVE: Beijing, China - 22 August 2026

ASSOCIATED PRESS
ARCHIVE: San Francisco, U.S. - 24 July 2026
6. Wide of delegates at San Francisco AI roundtable
7. Close of Dario Amodei, Anthropic CEO, speaking 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Beijing, China - 16 September 2026
++OVERLAYED BY 5, 6 AND 7++
8. SOUNDBITE (English) Da Wei, Director of the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University: 
“You said, let us slow down the development simultaneously. Theoretically, that's not a bad idea, maybe, but how to verify the other side has slowed? If I slow down, then maybe the other side, they will continue to develop their technology. So each side may view this suggestion as a kind of trap, because we don't trust each other.” 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
ARCHIVE: Beijing, China - 14 May 2026
9. Bilateral meeting between Xi and Trump

ASSOCIATED PRESS 

Beijing, China - 16 September 2026
++OVERLAYED BY 9,10 AND 11++
1-. SOUNDBITE (English) Da Wei, Director of the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University:
“This is two sides of one coin. You know, President Trump is a person so unconventional, so he, for good part, he can break those taboos. For bad part, he cannot, you know, have his idea be really implemented by the team. So we have to accept this coin.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
ARCHIVE: Beijing, China - 14 May 2026
11. Bilateral meeting between Xi and Trump
STORYLINE:
State visits usually occur when two countries are on warm terms, but U.S. President Donald Trump is hosting Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington this week as their economic and tech competition is only escalating, especially through an AI (artificial intelligence) race.

Xi's visit to Washington, which begins Wednesday, is his first in 10 years. It will also be the second meeting between Xi and Trump in six months, after they met in Beijing in May.

Their meeting comes after the two countries climbed down from last year's intense trade war, when they traded tit-for-tat sky-high tariffs that threatened the global economy.

China also choked off its world-leading supplies of critical minerals needed in products from electric cars to fighter jets.


The leaders now should produce deals that their governments can carry out, he said, noting that the two teams have "moved too slowly" since their summit in May, and that “we need to move fast.”

recentItems.title: Macron says he had 'great discussion' with Trump on Middle East and Ukraine ahead of UNGA
recentItems.description:
(22 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
New York - 21 September 2026
1. French President Emmanuel Macron walking
2. SOUNDBITE (French) Emmanuel Macron, French President:
"We had a great discussion that allowed us to talk about the crisis in the Middle East, and our determination to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and free up these stocks (of oil). We covered a number of solutions, and the diplomatic solutions that we're going to work on in the coming hours that would allow, without a global agreement, to let more oil tankers and container ships through. The other issue we discussed was the situation in the Red Sea – There's a growing confrontation and escalation there – and how to better secure oil terminals in the Red Sea."
++BLACK FRAMES++
3. SOUNDBITE (French) Emmanuel Macron, French President:
"We had a long conversation on Ukraine and Russia and the need to go stronger and faster in how we help our Ukrainian friends in terms of interceptors (missiles) which is a key aspect on the defensive front, and also, we revisited the initiatives we could take to find a moratorium on energy issues."
++BLACK FRAMES++
4. SOUNDBITE (French) Emmanuel Macron, French President:
"I had a very good discussion. It was very constructive. There was great availability. We were able to go into detail on these two conflicts which are obviously important for world peace and for our security, and which have a direct impact on the purchasing power of the French."
++BLACK FRAMES++
5. SOUNDBITE (French) Emmanuel Macron, French President:
"We will continue over the next few hours, and the goal is that in the coming days, indeed, we have ongoing progress even outside of New York. This trip can accelerate certain discussions, but we started talking before this, and we will continue in any case. I want results."
6. Macron walking into building
STORYLINE:
French President Emmanuel Macron said Monday night a “very constructive” meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump had opened up possible diplomatic paths towards reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Macron said this will allow more oil tankers through, in hopes that increased supplies will help bring down prices as France grapples with punishing inflation.

The two leaders met at Trump Tower in New York on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly. 

Macron said they had discussed solutions that could be pursued without waiting for a broader global agreement, with negotiations set to continue in the coming hours and possible progress within days.

Macron said the talks also covered mounting tensions in the Red Sea, the protection of oil terminals there and additional military support for Ukraine. 

Both conflicts, he said, have a direct impact on the purchasing power of French households. 

“I want results,” Macron said.
